title: Installing & Managing Releases 🚀
description: Deploy, upgrade, rollback, and uninstall apps with Helm.

slides.title: Installing a Chart 🛠️
slides.content:
# The `helm install` command

```bash
helm install <release-name> <chart> [flags]
```

Examples:
```bash
helm install my-nginx bitnami/nginx
helm install my-web bitnami/nginx --set service.type=ClusterIP
helm install prod-db bitnami/postgresql -f db-values.yaml
```

Each release is namespaced: `--namespace` or `-n`.

quizData.question: Which command installs a chart with a custom values file?

slides.title: Listing Releases 📋
slides.content:
## See what's installed

```bash
helm list                 # current namespace
helm list -A              # all namespaces
helm list --filter my-    # releases starting with 'my-'
helm list --failed        # only failed releases
```
Each release shows: name, namespace, revision, status, chart, app version.

slides.title: Release Status & History 📜
slides.content:
## Inspect a release

```bash
helm status my-nginx      # current state
helm history my-nginx     # all revisions
helm get values my-nginx  # user‑supplied values
helm get manifest my-nginx # full Kubernetes YAML applied
```

Use these for debugging and auditing.

quizData.question: Which command shows the rendered Kubernetes YAML for a release?
quizData.explanation: `helm get manifest <release>` outputs all resources created.

slides.title: Upgrading a Release ⬆️
slides.content:
## Change configuration or chart version

```bash
helm upgrade my-nginx bitnami/nginx --set service.type=NodePort
```

- Increments the revision number.
- Applies a patch (similar to `kubectl apply`).
- If you want to install if not exists: `helm upgrade --install my-nginx bitnami/nginx`.

slides.title: Upgrade Example
slides.codeSnippet:
# Update to a new chart version and change replicas
helm upgrade my-nginx bitnami/nginx --version 15.0.0 --set replicaCount=3

slides.title: Rolling Back a Release ↩️
slides.content:
## Undo a bad upgrade

```bash
helm rollback my-nginx 1      # rollback to revision 1
helm rollback my-nginx        # rollback to previous revision
```

This restores the release state from the selected revision. Helm keeps up to 10 revisions by default.

quizData.question: How do you revert a Helm release to its previous version?
quizData.explanation: `helm rollback <release>` goes to the previous revision.

slides.title: Uninstalling a Release 🗑️
slides.content:
## Clean up

```bash
helm uninstall my-nginx
```

Removes all Kubernetes resources created for that release, except hooks that may have opted out. Add `--keep-history` to preserve the release history for future rollback.
